paragraphs: Most automation stops at the part that produces the answer. The interesting problem is everything around it: what validates the output before anyone trusts it, what happens when it fails at 3am with nobody watching, and whether the next engineer reuses the pieces or rebuilds them. That is this role: build the Lego blocks, then make sure the people building the vehicles can actually use them.

At Corominas Consulting I owned the automation layer across roughly 85 deployments, building the shared Python packages each one composes, with behaviour carried in configuration rather than code branches so a new environment is a config change instead of a rebuild. I generated the orchestration instead of hand-building it: 26 workflow definitions and 490 nodes emitted by Python generators, so a policy change is a reviewable diff. These run unattended, so I wrote the deterministic validation layer that decides whether output is safe to ship at all: 18 checks across 10 families, backed by 715 assertion calls across 33 test scripts. Idempotency went in before retries did, and every destructive path is dry-run by default with snapshot and revert.

The enablement half is the part I enjoy most. I co-owned a repository with a domain lead who is not a software engineer: they authored the domain logic, I built the runtime that executes it, then pushed automation inside those units so each one self-encapsulates and the outer workflow consumes it as one block. They kept ownership of their work, and it got more reliable. At Formula Dream I built a meta-tool that generates importable workflow definitions pre-wired to a credential setup, taking an idea to a running workflow in under 10 minutes.

My first degree is mechanical engineering, so decomposing a physical problem into clean atomic functions is familiar ground rather than a stretch. SceneAgent, built in 48 hours, is that exercise: a point cloud goes in, DBSCAN clustering resolves 151 objects, and the geometry comes back out as atomic MCP tools an agent calls to locate something by description, measure a distance or plan a route, backed by pgvector and local embeddings.
I speak and write English at C2 and hold an EU Chancenkarte visa, so I am authorised to work in the Netherlands immediately with no sponsorship required.
